narratives.Description: bug(spec:render): renders only depth-1 of plan.items, discarding the phase/subphase/task tree make-spec.md mandates (+5 presentation defects)
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`spec:render` renders only the **first level** of `plan.items`. It never recurses into `item.items`, so the phase → subphase → task structure that [`templates/make-spec.md`](../blob/main/templates/make-spec.md) *instructs agents to author* is silently discarded — including the `Acceptance` and `Traces` narrative keys the renderer has dedicated handling for, because the template places those on the leaf task three levels down.

Following the framework's own documented authoring instructions produces a rendered specification containing a single heading per phase and nothing else.

Four further presentation defects are bundled below; all four reproduce from the same 30-line file.

**Environment:** `@deftai/directive` 0.117.0 (engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.117.0`), consumer project on macOS.

## Reproduction

`templates/make-spec.md` lines 118-146 give the required top-level structure. Copied **verbatim** into `spec.json`, with the single change noted below:

```json
{
  "xBRIEFInfo": { "version": "0.8" },
  "plan": {
    "title": "Project Name SPECIFICATION",
    "status": "approved",
    "narratives": {
      "Overview": "Brief project summary as a plain string.",
      "ProblemStatement": "Demonstrates the raw camelCase heading.",
      "Architecture": "System design as a plain string."
    },
    "items": [
      { "id": "phase-1", "title": "Phase 1: Foundation", "status": "pending",
        "items": [
          { "id": "1.1", "title": "Subphase 1.1: Setup", "status": "pending",
            "items": [
              { "id": "1.1.1", "title": "Task description", "status": "pending",
                "narrative": { "Acceptance": "...", "Traces": "FR-1" } }
            ] }
        ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

```
deft spec-render spec.json OUT.md
```

**Actual output, in full:**

```markdown
# Project Name SPECIFICATION

## Overview

Brief project summary as a plain string.

## ProblemStatement

Demonstrates the raw camelCase heading.

## Architecture

System design as a plain string.

## phase-1: Phase 1: Foundation  `[pending]`
```

Subphase `1.1`, task `1.1.1`, and its `Acceptance` and `Traces` are all gone.

## Defect 1 — no recursion into nested items (primary)

`dist/render/spec-render.js:148-149` iterates `plan.items` with a flat `for` loop and never descends:

```js
if (Array.isArray(items)) {
    for (const item of items) {
```

Within that one level it *does* render detail — `**Depends on**` from `metadata.dependencies`, `**Traces**`, and `Acceptance` split into bullets (lines 157-180). So the capability exists; it simply cannot reach the depth at which `make-spec.md` says the data lives.

The contradiction is internal to the framework:

- `make-spec.md:191` — "Break into phases, subphases, tasks"
- `make-spec.md:124-140` — required JSON shows three levels, `narrative: {Acceptance, Traces}` on the leaf
- `make-spec.md:184-190` — documents the rendered output as containing `#### Subphase 1.1` and `- Task 1.1.1: (description, traces: FR-1, dependencies, acceptance criteria)`

None of that output shape is produced.

**This is not #1566.** That issue was scoped to *lifecycle scope aggregation* from `vbrief/{pending,active,completed}` — "appends an `Implementation Plan` section generated from all lifecycle folders". Its acceptance criteria never mention `plan.items`, and `commands.md:247` documents the compact default as "no lifecycle Scope outlook, no `LegacyArtifacts`" only. The item-tree limitation appears to be independent and undocumented.

**Consumer impact.** A consumer specification with six phases and ~40 tasks renders as six bare headings. The only way to get a readable document today is to duplicate task titles, statuses and dependencies into each phase's `narrative` prose — deliberate data duplication against the item tree that is supposed to be the source of truth, with the drift risk that implies.

## Defect 2 — the template's own example is refused by the renderer

`make-spec.md:120` specifies `"status": "proposed"`. The renderer rejects it:

```
⚠ specification.vbrief.json status is 'proposed' (expected one of approved, running, completed)
```

The repro above only renders because I changed `proposed` → `approved`. An agent following the template verbatim gets a hard stop. Either `RENDERABLE_SPEC_STATUSES` should include `proposed`, or the template should not specify it.

## Defect 3 — heading stutter, straight from the documented example

Line 156 emits `## ${itemId}: ${titleText}`, and `make-spec.md` titles its example item `"Phase 1: Foundation"` under id `"phase-1"`. The documented input therefore renders as:

```markdown
## phase-1: Phase 1: Foundation  `[pending]`
```

Either the id prefix or the convention of repeating it in the title has to go.

## Defect 4 — canonical narrative keys render as raw camelCase headings

`SPECIFICATION_NARRATIVE_KEY_ORDER` is `["Overview", "ProblemStatement", "Goals", "UserStories", "Requirements", "SuccessMetrics", "EdgeCases", "Architecture", "TechDecisions", "ImplementationPhases", "PreImplementationGates"]`, and the key is used as the heading verbatim — so a spec using the canonical vocabulary gets `## ProblemStatement`, `## ImplementationPhases`, `## PreImplementationGates`. A presentable document needs "Problem statement", "Implementation phases", "Pre-implementation gates". A display-name map would fix it without changing the key contract.

## Defect 5 — section order cannot be controlled without abandoning the canonical keys

Canonical keys render first in fixed order; every other key is then emitted **alphabetically** (lines 137-144). An author using domain-appropriate section names has no way to order them except by choosing names that happen to sort correctly. In our spec I ended up naming sections "Decisions settled", "Dependencies and sequencing", "Implementation phases", "Open decisions and gates", "Source and confidence" — chosen so alphabetical order coincides with reading order. That is a workaround, not a design.

## Defect 6 — dependency field is undocumented and contradicts the template

Lines 157-166 read dependencies from `metadata.dependencies`, falling back to `item.dependencies`. Neither is in `xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json`'s `PlanItem` definition, and `make-spec.md:190` shows dependencies as *prose* inside the task description ("dependencies, acceptance criteria") and as `(depends on: 1.1)` appended to a heading. An author following the template writes dependencies where nothing can read them; the field that *is* read is documented nowhere.

## Suggested fix

1. Recurse into `item.items`, mapping depth to heading level (`##` → `###` → `####`), matching `make-spec.md:184-192`. Keep the existing per-item `Depends on` / `Traces` / `Acceptance` handling at every depth.
2. Add `proposed` to renderable statuses, or correct the template.
3. Stop prefixing the id when the title already begins with it, or drop the prefix and render the id as metadata.
4. Add a display-name map for canonical narrative keys.
5. Give authors explicit section ordering — an optional `narrativeOrder` array, or render unknown keys in insertion order rather than alphabetically.
6. Add `dependencies` to the `PlanItem` schema and document it in `make-spec.md`.
7. Add a regression test that renders the `make-spec.md` example verbatim and asserts subphase and task content survive.

Items 1 and 2 are the blocking ones. 3-6 are presentation and contract clarity, but they compound: together they make the default rendered artifact hard to hand to a human reviewer, which is the artifact's whole purpose.

## Willing to contribute

Happy to open a PR for the recursion fix and the regression test if the approach above is the direction you'd want.

## Gate stamp

The triage author stamps the semantic call. This write-back is the round-1 ceiling.

P1 is the silent discard of nested plan.items (Defect 1). Defects 2-6 are bundled presentation/contract issues on the same renderer; they are in-envelope as issue body, not extra pain ids.

model: claude-opus-5
```quarantined
role: critic
```

Round 1, open critique, fresh critic. Every anchor below re-verified against `git show 64667b94a6afd263c0d70791be44175fd72bd65c:<path>`, not from the reported `dist/` line numbers.

P1 reproduces at source. `renderSpecMarkdown` (`packages/core/src/render/spec-render.ts`) iterates `plan.items` with one flat `for` loop, reads `id`/`title`/`status`, `metadata.dependencies`, `narrative.Traces` and `narrative.Acceptance`, and never touches `item.items`. The tree is discarded. The rest of this post is about what the fix as scoped does not reach.

### F1 -- the named command is not the one contract-conformant consumers run

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence. `content/strategies/v0-20-contract.md:88` carries the prohibition on invoking `task spec:render` on a greenfield tree that lacks `specification.vbrief.json`, and routes to `task project:export-spec` instead. Same prohibition at `content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md:881` and `content/strategies/speckit.md:144`. The sanctioned emitter is `exportSpec` (`packages/core/src/render/export-spec.ts`, #2013 / #1502). Grepping that file for `items` returns nothing. It composes banner, title, `renderNarrativeSections(narratives)`, and an optional scope-outlook section. It renders no plan item at any depth.

Failure mode. Recursion lands in `renderSpecMarkdown`. A v0.20 consumer follows the contract, runs `task project:export-spec`, and gets a SPECIFICATION.md with zero phases and zero tasks -- strictly worse than the six bare headings this issue reports, and untouched by the fix.

Disposition consequence. P1 relief cannot bind for the population the contract routes to the other command. Either the target widens to both emitters, or the write-back records explicitly that P1 is scoped to legacy migrated trees holding `specification.*brief.json`.

### F2 -- the proposed depth-to-heading map does not produce the shape it cites, and the proposed test cannot tell

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence. Suggested fix 1 asks for `##` then `###` then `####`, "matching make-spec.md:184-192". The block it cites is titled **SPECIFICATION Structure (Light path -- embedded Requirements)**. It places phases at `###` under a `## Implementation Plan` wrapper, subphases at `####`, and the task as a **bullet** carrying description, traces, dependencies and acceptance inline: `- Task 1.1.1: (description, traces: FR-1, dependencies, acceptance criteria)`. Fix 1 produces phases at `##`, no wrapper, leaf tasks as `####` headings, and Acceptance as separate bullets via `splitAcceptance`.

Failure mode. The patch ships, suggested fix 7 (render the make-spec.md example verbatim and assert subphase and task content survive) passes, and the rendered document still does not match the documented structure. The internal contradiction the issue opens with is half-closed, and no test discriminates the remainder.

Disposition consequence. "Recurse" is underdetermined. The design has to state which of the two shapes is authoritative before a mechanism is picked.

### F3 -- one-key recursion does not fix the class, and the class is already live next door

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence. Schema `$defs.PlanItem` (`packages/types/schemas/xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json`) declares **both** `items` ("Preferred v0.6 nested PlanItem field") and `subItems` ("Deprecated legacy alias for items; retained for compatibility"). Fix 1 names `item.items` only.

The repo already has a convention for this. `packages/core/src/render/spec-validate.ts:36` iterates the nested-key pair `["items", "subItems"]` and recurses; `packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-consistency.ts:123` uses the same pair. `validateSpec` is called by `renderSpecMarkdown` before it renders -- so the render pipeline already walks the whole tree to validate it, then throws the tree away.

Inventory of the four item-consuming emitters at this SHA:

| emitter | nesting behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `spec-render.ts` | flat, depth 1, `items` only |
| `scope-outlook.ts:165` | flat, depth 1, `items` only |
| `export-spec.ts` | no items at all |
| `roadmap-render.ts:161` | recurses -- into `subItems` only, never `item.items` |

Failure mode, two limbs. First: a legacy migrated tree authored with `subItems` -- the population `v0-20-contract.md:87` still permits to run `spec:render` -- renders bare headings after the fix. Second, and larger: `roadmap-render.ts` is the mirror image. It descends the deprecated alias and drops the preferred key, so a make-spec.md-conformant spec loses every subphase and task in ROADMAP.md today. That is the same defect class, already shipped, on a renderer this issue does not name.

Disposition consequence. Patching one loop leaves four nesting conventions in one directory. The mechanism should be a shared dual-key walk reused from the `spec-validate` convention, and the target should say whether `roadmap-render` is in or out.

### F4 -- the branch being changed has no test at all, and the authoring side is contract-pinned while the rendering side is not

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence. Every `renderSpecMarkdown` / `renderSpec` fixture in the repo uses an empty item array -- `render.test.ts` (lines 42, 52, 96, 114, 131, 459, 492, 520), `spec-authority.test.ts`, `verify-source/spec-prd-fresh.test.ts`, `content-contracts/skills/machine_generated_banner.test.ts`. The item branch -- the dependency line, the traces line, and `splitAcceptance` -- is exercised by nothing.

Meanwhile `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/decomposition_readiness.test.ts:98-106` requires make-spec.md to teach that nested children within a PlanItem must use `items`, and to not contain the deprecated alias spelling.

Failure mode. The issue's reading that "the capability exists; it simply cannot reach the depth" is a source reading, not verified behaviour -- nothing has ever run it. A recursion patch is therefore not a guarded refactor, and fix 7 is the first test of the branch.

Disposition consequence. The authoring contract is pinned and the rendering contract is absent. That asymmetry is the mechanism-level cause of P1, not the loop itself. The durable remedy is a paired contract test that renders the pinned template example and asserts output shape, plus coverage of the existing depth-1 handlers; a single fixture asserting that task text is present restores nothing.

### F5 -- two of the bundled dispositions point the wrong way

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence, Defect 2. `RENDERABLE_SPEC_STATUSES` is the set approved / running / completed (`packages/core/src/render/constants.ts:121`) while `VALID_STATUSES` includes `proposed`. That set has already been widened once deliberately, for `completed` (`xbrief/completed/2026-04-15-spec-render-completed-status.xbrief.json`, "status gate rejects 'completed' specs -- overly strict for post-implementation projects"), and #432 made rendering the speckit Phase 3 to Phase 4 human review gate.

Failure mode. Admitting `proposed` lets an unreviewed spec render as the artifact the review gate consumes, inverting the gate. The two options in Defect 2 are not equivalent; the template correction is the cheap one and already sits under a content contract that would carry it.

Evidence, Defect 6. `plan.edges` is a declared, typed dependency mechanism (`$defs.Edge`, `Plan.properties.edges`), and `roadmap-render.ts:99-109` builds its dep map from it -- which is where the `(depends on: 1.1)` shape at make-spec.md:190 actually comes from. The `metadata.dependencies` / `item.dependencies` read in `spec-render` is the undeclared outlier; `dependencies` is absent from `PlanItem.properties` and only validates because `additionalProperties` is true.

Failure mode. Fix 6 promotes the ad-hoc field into the schema, making two typed dependency representations permanent and leaving the two renderers reading different fields.

Disposition consequence. Converge `spec-render` onto `plan.edges` with the ad-hoc read kept as compat, and take the template correction for Defect 2 -- or record why the review gate should admit pre-approval specs.

### F6 -- verbosity has to fail closed, or this re-opens #1566

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence. The #1566 remedy was compact-by-default (`DEFAULT_INCLUDE_SCOPES_MODE` set to off, `constants.ts`). The countervailing principle is recorded in the same module, `spec-render.ts:41-42`: callers must fail closed rather than silently omitting content.

Failure mode. Full three-level recursion with per-leaf Acceptance bullets pushes back toward the #1566 shape on a long-lived project; a silent depth cap added to avoid that is exactly the silent omission the module already calls a P1.

Disposition consequence. Name the control and make it mirror `normalizeIncludeScopesMode` -- explicit mode, unknown tokens throw. Do not leave depth unbounded and do not truncate quietly.

### F7 -- injection lens

`footnote`

The lens fires: this renderer consumes agent-authored JSON that can originate from ingested issue text, and writes a document later agents read as the spec. Values reach markdown through a bare string coercion, so a `title` or narrative containing a newline and a hash character forges a heading today at depth 1. Recursion does not create the surface, but it multiplies the sites, and fix 1 puts author-controlled strings in heading position at three depths. The write path is already hardened (`containedWrite`, #3953). The deterministic control, if wanted, is escaping a line-start hash in interpolated values -- the same instinct the arc-record reserved line-starts already encode. Recorded so it is not met later as new.

### Road not taken

I considered classifying F1 as `sharpens-framing`, on the grounds that the reporter demonstrably runs `spec:render` and `v0-20-contract.md:87` still permits it for migrated trees, so relief is real for them. I put it at blocking because the issue's stated impact is that duplicating task data into phase narratives is "the only way to get a readable document today", and a relief claim scoped to the legacy command will read as satisfying that while the sanctioned command still emits nothing. What flips it: a write-back amendment scoping P1 explicitly to legacy migrated trees. That turns F1 into a scope note.

### Steelman

The strongest rejected position is that `spec:render` is legacy, so patch it minimally and stop. It is defensible -- it is the reporter's actual path, the patch is small, and item omission in `exportSpec` may be deliberate, a stakeholder-audience export of narratives only. If that intent is recorded anywhere, F1 collapses to a footnote. I looked for it: `resolveExportScopePolicy` governs the scope-outlook section only, and nothing I read states that dropping the item tree is intended. Absent that record, the silent-omission principle at `spec-render.ts:41-42` reads against it.

Recursing that one loop does not close it: the command contract consumers actually run does not emit items at all, the cited heading map is not the documented shape, and a one-key walk leaves roadmap-render as the mirror-image bug.

Confirming this map recuts first-ship to a shared dual-key walk and names which emitter and which output shape are in. It does not close by patching one flat loop.

This is not an instruction to a later builder.

model: claude-opus-5
```quarantined
role: critic
```

audit-targets: pain-P1

Stop 4 pain-audit, round 2, fresh critic. Target: `relieves: P1` on successor lean 5686380064. Denominator: write-back 5685863527 -- "P1 is the silent discard of nested plan.items (Defect 1)". Every anchor below re-read with `git show 64667b94a6afd263c0d70791be44175fd72bd65c:<path>`.

**Verdict: `relieves: P1` is not established as written.** One clause of the Bound remedy does bind real relief -- item 3's shared dual-key walk, applied to `renderSpecMarkdown`, ends the discard for the reporter's own command. Two things defeat the cite anyway: the control the remedy names is off-by-default in the exemplar it names, and item 1 offers a branch that discharges P1 by re-scoping it from a surface that does not own the denominator.

### F1 -- the depth control's default is unnamed, and the exemplar the remedy names defaults to off

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence. Bound-remedy item 6 asks for "an explicit depth/verbosity control that fails closed on unknown tokens, mirroring include-scopes". Include-scopes is `DEFAULT_INCLUDE_SCOPES_MODE = "off"` (`packages/core/src/render/constants.ts:40`). The fail-closed property the item names is the unknown-token branch of `tryParseIncludeScopesMode` (`spec-render.ts:41-44`, returns `undefined` on an unrecognised token); it is not a statement about the default. The module's recorded principle in that same comment is broader than the item quotes it -- "callers MUST fail closed rather than silently omitting content (#1566 Greptile P1)" -- and that principle cuts toward nested-on. The remedy imports the exemplar, not the principle.

Failure mode. Builder lands the dual-key walk plus `--depth` mirroring include-scopes, default off. The reporter re-runs the repro verbatim -- `deft spec-render spec.json OUT.md`, no flags -- and gets the same six bare headings. The contract test at item 4 does not discriminate: if it passes a depth token it goes green while the default path stays broken; if it passes none it contradicts the default it was written under.

Disposition consequence. A silence complaint is not relieved by a walk that runs only when the user already knows a flag exists. Bind the default explicitly (nested on, with the #1566 compaction pressure carried by a raisable cap rather than an off switch), or record that P1 relief is flag-gated -- which the write-back's "silent discard" wording does not permit. Until the default is on the lean, `relieves: P1` is conditional on a value nobody has written down.

### F2 -- item 1's second branch edits the pain denominator from a surface that does not own it

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence. Pain coverage (#4496) in `content/contracts/design-critique.md`: "The latest Stop 1 write-back ... owns the denominator" and "A superseding warrant is a new Stop 1, not last-writer prose elsewhere on the thread." Bound-remedy item 1 is a disjunction whose second branch is "record that P1 is scoped to legacy `specification.*brief.json` trees only". That branch does not relieve P1; it shrinks it. The excluded population is real and verified: `packages/core/src/render/export-spec.ts` contains the token `items` zero times at this SHA -- it renders no plan item at any depth -- and `content/strategies/v0-20-contract.md:88` forbids `task spec:render` on a greenfield tree, routing it to `task project:export-spec`.

Failure mode. The harvest is literal capture: `extractBoundRemedyHarvest` -> `parseListItems`, mapped at `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts:1483` to `{ title, status }`. The builder reads item 1, takes the cheaper branch, writes the scope note, and the bind conjunct is satisfied while `task project:export-spec` still emits zero phases and zero tasks for the population the contract routes there. Round 1 F1 was taken `accept-into-contract` on exactly that population being inside the pain; permitting a remedy branch that scopes it back out reverses the accepted take without a `disagree`.

Disposition consequence. Resolve the branch on the lean. If branch B is the intent, it is a new Stop 1 write-back that restates the denominator, and relief is re-cited against that -- not a bullet on a successor map. `relieves: P1` cannot be graded true while P1 extent is one of the remedy own open choices.

### F3 -- "reused from spec-validate" names a walker that is not exported

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence. `packages/core/src/render/spec-validate.ts` exports three things: `ValidateSpecResult`, `validateSpec(specPath)`, `main`. The dual-key recursion is module-private `validatePlanItem` (`spec-validate.ts:36`, `for (const nestedKey of ["items", "subItems"] as const)`), and it accumulates error strings -- it yields no traversal a renderer could consume. The one exported entry point takes a path, re-reads and re-parses the file, and returns `[ok, msg]`. `renderSpecMarkdown` already calls it that way at `spec-render.ts:113`, which is why the pipeline walks the whole tree and then discards it.

Failure mode. A builder taking item 3 literally finds nothing importable and re-implements the key pair inline.
